chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from the one who mentioned it, from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Karram, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'If the people were only two men, one of the two would be the Imam.'
And he said: 'The last one to die would be the Imam, lest anyone argue against God, Mighty and Majestic, that He left him without a divine authority of God upon him.'

key_terms.الْإِمَامَ: The Imam — the divinely appointed religious and political authority in Shia Islam
key_terms.حُجَّةٍ: Hujjah — divine proof, authority, or argument; in Shia theology, refers to the Imam as God's proof upon creation
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic — a common honorific for God (Azza wa Jalla)
key_terms.يَحْتَجَّ: To argue or protest — the idea of presenting a counter-argument before God on the Day of Judgment

ai.seo_question: Why does Imam al-Sadiq say the last person to die would be the Imam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes through two complementary statements the absolute necessity of the Imam's existence at all times. The first statement — that even if only two people existed, one would be the Imam — affirms that the Imamate is not contingent on a minimum population threshold. The second statement provides the theological rationale: God's justice requires that no human being be left without a hujjah (divine proof/authority), for to leave someone without guidance would provide them a valid excuse before God on the Day of Judgment. This doctrine reflects the Shia principle that the earth is never empty of an Imam.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from the one who mentioned it, from Al Hassan Bin Musa Al Khashhab, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad, from Karram who said,
‘Abu Abdllah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If the people were (only) two men, it would be so that one of the two would be the Imam<sup>asws</sup>’.

And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The last one to be dying would be the Imam<sup>asws</sup>, lest anyone could argue against Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic that He<sup>azwj</sup> Left him to be without a Divine Authority of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> upon him’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from those who he has mentioned from al-Hassan ibn Musa al-Khashshab from Ja’far ibn Muhammad from Kiram from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.
“If of all the people there will remain only two man one of them will be the Imam.
He also said, ‘The last person to die will be the Imam (a.s.) so that no one could complain against Allah leaving him without Imam, the person with Divine authority over him.’”
